notes.title: A massive missile strike against Ukraine - 10th October 2022 Dev update
notes.notes:
Hello

We are here today with an urgent report about the massive missile attack against cities all over Ukraine, including the capital Kyiv, where our team is located. This is how the day started for us:


Part of the team was already in the office, while other were getting ready to go to work or en route, when the first missiles hit Kyiv in the morning of October 10th. That was followed with several more rounds of attack. Overall, it was reported that 83 missiles of different types (43 shot down by AA defenses) and some kamikaze drones (some say 9 out of 10 destroyed by AA) were deployed in this attack. 

We decided that everyone could work from home, although some people were already at the office. That came in handy, as subway stopped for a few hours. 

As a person who lives in Kyiv my whole life and knows the city quite well, I can tell you that most places of the reported attacks does not make any sense in terms of military logic - its just some parks, squares or cars in the middle of the street, some tourist places as well. Nothing like an important military target, or even government building… The only explanation to that could be that the aim of these attacks is terror of civilians and an attempt to sow panic and chaos. 

Yet, some strikes did hit some power plants across the country, causing power shortages in several large cities (but not in Kyiv). Right now, I am writing this news update in my apartments in Kyiv, not knowing where the next Russian missiles would land…

Ukraine War Stories tells the story of the first month of the war. It would take more than one game to tell the story of this entire war… Still, if you want to know how everything started for the civilian people of Ukraine back in February - join us for the full release of our free title on 18 October 2022. 

The story of this war is far from over. Stand united, support Ukraine! 

With Best Regards from Kyiv
Oleksandr and the Starni Games team

notes.title: 8 Days to Release - Douglas A-1 Skyraider The US Attack Aircraft
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/735bfbb3c9f0ef7335b2984bba27902e6dad1c28.png

In the age of the turbojet, Douglas A-1 Skyraider flew as a piston-powered, propeller-driven blast from the past. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/12bda2c534d744d6812578cee65c8d21ee4a0737.jpg

With the rapid development of jet aircraft towards the end of the war, dozens, if not hundreds of piston engine aircraft became obsolete. The Skyraider could have joined their lot, but its innovative turbo-compound engine gave it a chance to prove itself - and prove itself it did.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/500fbb2065c7709ed3a10144dbf984b50aac36e8.jpg

A solid, well-made and innovative at a time, Douglas A-1 would last well into the Vietnam War, only decommissioned in the 1970s. It was an attack aircraft that could shred ground targets with its 20-mm autocannons, carry out tactical bombings (with its payload capacity of 3600 kg) and deliver torpedo strikes equally well.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/474ae69218b59df3733695829d035bdb30e3b894.jpg

There is no telling how effective Douglas A-1 would have been in WWII if it were finalized and deployed faster. And in Fight for Freedom, you’ll get to explore that exact possibility.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/5118c29e7556e9dbbae33d83f371a28db1a6c3fd.png

Victory in Europe Day

General! We would like to celebrate V-E Day by uploading a new Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom Demo build for free. So, now everyone can enjoy the game and live through the epochal events, such as the Normandy landings.

We are immensely grateful to all the valiant soldiers who fought in WW2 and brought the World age of peace and prosperity. Now, we can see the horrors of massive conflicts only in games, and we get to choose which games to play. We think there is a lot to be learned about our society and human nature in general by studying the events of WW2 - and what better way of immersing oneself in these events than to become an active participant, even if only in the game. 

The New Demo

The new Demo has around 5 hours of gameplay - the first operations of both the UK and the US campaigns. Overall the build runs great and there should not be any serious technical issues. There is some stuff that we still have to iron out, especially in localizations and cinematics, so the most vigilant players may notice some issues, but we are working day and night to correct everything before release, so do not worry - we will do our best to correct all possible shortcomings. In fact, if you notice anything weird - make sure to let us know at our community hub - and we will do our best to fix it asap. 

The Game Release - 21 May

The full game will be released on 21 May 2021, so there are only two weeks left. Wishlist Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom, so that you do not miss its launch. 

📍 Important notes: 
 You can use Demo save files when you play the full game. So, you could covert your Demo progress into a full game on its full launch on 21 May.
 You can post any materials without restrictions.

notes.title: Update 3.08. Strategic Mind Anniversary 🛠
notes.notes:
Admiral! Two years have passed since the Strategic Mind series began with an Early Access for the Strategic Mind: The Pacific on 30 April 2019. It has been a magnificent two years full of events and new releases. We would like to celebrate the Strategic Mind second anniversary - and what better way to celebrate there is, other than deliver a new update? 😉

The majority of the changes were based on the feedback and reports of the community - so we could not have done it without you. We will keep improving the series and with your help, we can deliver much better results and turn the series into every wargamer’s dream. We will keep looking for your feedback and suggestions and continue to develop the series.

So, here we are with all the hottest fixes and features from the upcoming Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom.

Update 3.08

New content:

 Fully reworked naval combat tutorial - now it consists of 3 parts. 
 Overhauled 5-parts of the land operations tutorial, but the content is the same.
 All tutorial operations now work much better. It was hard to click certain hexes/units in tutorials before, and now these issues were fixed. 
Game mechanic changes: 
 Overwatch fire now does take into account Line of sight. (Before it was only Spotting and Gun range). So, now the anti-tank guns can no longer Overwatch you “through” the building, city or forest, etc. They can only Overwatch you where they would have been able to fire normally.   

Quality of life improvements:
 Added special “+” Overstrength indicator showing when each unit is eligible for an Overstrength.
 The terrain info screen now has two additional pieces of information: Line of Fire (Yes/No) and Combat penalty (Yes/No). 
 Added a “New hero available” notification when you get a new hero. You will see a flying label (similar to the “Level up available” one).
 Added hint to unit price when purchasing units with all the discount information so now you can see more clearly how different global bonuses, awards, and other things affect the final unit price. 
Changes:

 Infantry with Heavy equipment and no ground transport now cannot be deployed. (As it cannot move) The corresponding message box with an explanation is added. 
 Changed prices for Anti-aircraft guns equipment: Small searchlight now costs 10 Prestige, Medium searchlight - 20, Heavy searchlight - 30, Radar - 50.
 Fixed issue when boarding of the ground transport would not be displayed in a hex if there is enemy infrastructure. 
 Now, when the unit has no series, the “Series: none” is displayed.
 Moved the “Pause after every line” option was moved from Game Settings to Sound Settings.
Fixes:
 Fixed the replenishment of equipment charges not working properly in some cases. Now you always get the charges replenished in the Service zone if you are eligible (Have the supply). 
 Fixed exploit with Undo button: you can no longer use Undo after changing the unit’s equipment. 
 Fixed exploit with Undo button: you can no longer gain extra movement by Using Undo after Close combat movement. 
 Fixed crash with Undo button during landing or take off - now it is unavailable after these actions.
 Fixed a rare issue that would lead to incorrect Line of Fire calculation in some cases.  
 Fixed an annoying sound that often happened during the loading screens. 

Misc:
 Corrected the Close quarters flying label “close defense” -> “close quarters” in all languages. 


This is not the end

Looking forward to more feedback.

Undo move
Added the “Undo move” button. It allows you to retrace your unit's last movement. It is eligible, only if you want to change your last movement and the movement did not affect the current tactical situation. It is not eligible if: an attack happened, the spotting has changed, the objective status has changed, the unit embarked/disembarked, etc.

We are working on optimizing the game performance. So, far we successfully implemented a number of improvements. Some are still underway and will be added in future updates, as we keep working on the Strategic Mind series.

notes.title: Update 3.00 is now live!
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/1299ab5901cb258182ddeda914bd39350c16d74a.png
Update 3.00

Steam achievements added!
You asked us to add Steam achievements since the game release. It did take us quite a while, but finally, the achievements are live. We hope that you will enjoy the additional reward for the sophisticated and large-scale operations of Strategic Mind: The Pacific.

Steam cloud saves
Finally, your saves files will be stored in the Steam cloud. So, you no longer risk losing them and can easily transfer them to another device.

Better Steam integration

 Now, you can change the language in Steam settings before you launch the game.
 Also, now your Steam language is set as the game language by default.

New set of controls
Now there is a new set of controls ("Modern") set by default. The old controls are now "Legacy" controls. You can change between the two in the Settings->Game->Controls section. 
Modern:
Unit selection - Left mouse button
Attack/Movement - Right mouse button
Open unit info - Middle (wheel) mouse button (or "I" hotkey)
Legacy:
Unit selection - Left mouse button
Attack/Movement - Left mouse button
Open unit info - Right mouse button

Added ground combat tutorials from the Blitzkrieg
Added 5-part tutorial in ground combat, supplied, infrastructure, etc. 

Revamped UI with new features

 Improved design and usability
 You can now enter custom names for your units (and save files)
 You can see the day/night cycle and the current date (icon in the top right corner)
 Improved the Manual UI

New equipment
 Sniper squad
 Molotov cocktail
 Smoke grenade
 Spaced armor
 Searchlights (small, medium, big) 

Equipment changes
Now incendiary bomb/shells and armor-piercing bombs/shells cost 0 Prestige to install on your unit, but instead each time you use them you have to spend:
3 Prestige for an Incendiary shell
5 Prestige for an Armor-piercing shell
5 Prestige for an Incendiary bomb
5 Prestige for an Armor-piercing bomb

Recon units can now use mortars and recoilless guns
Slight changes in various equipment stats and cost

Gameplay changes:
 Reworked AI (it is less "suicidal" now). 
 If the unit has already attacked this turn it cannot change Equipment until the end of turn.
 Reinforcement no longer costs Command points (only Prestige). Prestige cost is now x2 of what you would have had to spend at the end of the operation. (On default settings 40% of unit cost (it was 50% before)). 
 Removed experience cap (per turn) for all units
 Increased the experience required to gain a 2-5th level
 The maximum level for heroes is lowered from 10 to 5 (If you already had high-level heroes they will remain as before with all the skills, but will not be able to level up further. Also, their stats bonus is capped at +5.)
 Now killing an enemy unit with a hero gives +50 Exp instead of +10.

New settings
 You can now set the Unit speech volume separately from other sources
 Fixed disable/enable hex grid option

New hotkeys
 H; Show/hide hex grid
 I; Show Unit info screen of the selected unit
 Alt; Show unit outlines (if disabled)

notes.title: Update 2.06
notes.notes:
In today’s update 2.06 we fix more issues reported by the community and improved German localization.

Changes:
 Corrected all German “technical localization” (all the abilities, ship parts descriptions, etc.) There might still be some things to fix with the new version, which we will address in later updates, but over we expect the quality of localization to increase dramatically. Next, we will work on fixing German subtitles for cinematics. If you play the game with German localization on, please do let us know what you think about these fixes.
 We made some changes to the Australia deployment phase: now you have only 4 deploy hexes in each location, representing the fact that not the whole fleet was able to reach Australia in time. You can deploy the rest of your units in the second deploy phase before turn 2. Additionally, we moved some of the enemy forces further away to balance out the increase in the difficulty of the objective to cover the Army landing. 
 Adjusted the stats of Japanese Ground transports, as some of them were incorrect. Additionally, the USA Ground transport LVT-4 now adds 2 Soft attack and 1 Hard attack as it had guns mounted on it.
 Fixed an occasional tutorial issue when the player could not press the “Acquire” button (Reported by ChiefCommander33, and others). (It was quite hard to replicate, as it was not happening on any of the PCs in our office. Luckily, one of our friends has encountered it on her laptop and allowed us to borrow it for a few days. Even then it was hard to figure it out). 
 Fixed important crash (reported by [CHN]Zephyr), which was happening after an Infantry unit spent all its movement points, then got new Ground transport, and it could still move on the transport causing a crash. Another variant of the same issue was crash after the Infantry with transport got overrun and was shown ineligible hexes to move to, and if the player chose to move there the game would crash.
 Fix an issue with Japanese campaign 05 operation (reported by Nix), where completing objectives in a certain order would cause a crash.
 Fix an issue with Japanese campaign 05 operation, the objective to pursue the enemy fleet was working incorrectly.
 Fixed USA campaign 04 operation secondary objective to kill submarines not giving experience to your Destroyers as a part of the reward. (Reported by Tim)
 Fixed USA campaign 06 operation secondary objective to capture the place where Marines barracks were not giving experience to your Marines as a part of the reward. (Reported by The Matrix has you!)
 Fixed Japan campaign 05 operation secondary objective to prevent Zero capture, the turn timer was going up instead of going down.
 Fixed a rare bug in Japanese campaign 08 operation, where you would fail secondary objective even if you captured oil storages. (Reported by aramoor50, thank you for the save files)
 Fixed some visual elements on the map (eg. railroad on bridges etc) on several maps. 
 Fixed incorrect text in Japanese campaign 06 operations the secondary objective “capture the airfield at Munda” -> “Hold the airfield at Munda”. (Reported by Night_Phoenix)
 Fixed dialogue when first attacking Tekketsu Kinotai in USA campaign operation 09. 
 In the Japanese campaign 06 operation we moved the completion of the main objective to hold all victory hexes one turn earlier so that you do not get a warning that you have the last turn before indecision penalty kicks in even though you did everything perfectly.

We would like to thank all of our community members who keep reporting all the occurring issues and help us to make the game better. We do appreciate your help. Additionally, we would like to thank Night Phoenix for his Lets play series covering the Japanese campaign, as it also helped us to identify and fix a couple of issues. 

We will keep improving and polishing the game. Our team wishes everyone good holidays. Stay tuned as there are some big announcements coming. 

With best regards
Starni Games development team

As many of you could have guessed, cutscenes require lots of effort. We have already done the script and other preliminary work, however, there are still much to do in this regard. So we do not expect them to be ready before the full release.

The similar situation exists regarding the voice acting. We have to finalise all the lines before making and implementing voice acting.

All units and rewards for Early access are already in the game. As well as most of the skills.

HQ skills, equipment and icons are work in progress.

Core mechanics are ready, but require additional testing and polishing both before and after the beginning of Early access stage.
Day/night and rain features are now being tested.

We plan to add heroes after the beginning of Early access as the work progresses and we deal with more crucial elements of the game.

We hope that this portion of content will help you understand what to expect from the Full version of the game (apart from cutscenes). And, on the other hand, your feedback would help us make the Full version even better.

We want our development process to be as transparent as possible without spoiling too much of the actual game. We want you to be informed about our work, but at the same time keep some surprises in store for the time when you will finally be able to launch the game.
